name: Form Validation Pattern - UX and Timing Strategies
description: When form errors appear, what they say, and where focus goes: errors when someone leaves a field they typed in or tries to submit, never while they type or tab through; an error summary for longer forms; one announcement per error; and the browser's constraint validation working with the project's form library or without one.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Make a form's errors appear at the right time, say how to fix them, and reach everyone: show format errors when someone leaves a field they typed in, show "required" errors only after a submit attempt, clear an error as soon as it's fixed, and on a failed submit move focus to an error summary or the first invalid field. Apply this with the project's form library and schema library when it has them; otherwise use the browser's constraint validation with the app's own messages. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: Format errors when someone leaves a field they typed in; "required" errors only after a submit attempt; no errors while someone types or tabs through
Once a field shows an error, it is checked on every input, so the error goes as soon as it is fixed
A section that doesn't apply is hidden and disabled, so it never blocks the submit
After a reset that wasn't cancelled, everything worked out from the values is rebuilt from the restored values, as on page load
A failed submit moves focus to an error summary with links to the fields on longer forms, or to the first invalid field on short ones
Errors in text next to their fields, with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and no live regions on field errors
The submit button enabled until sending starts, then aria-disabled with focus kept
The browser's constraint validation with novalidate set from script, so it still works without script
Async checks after a pause, with only the latest answer counting, and no checks that reveal private facts
Multi-step forms with focus on each step's heading and no repeated questions (WCAG 2.2 3.3.7)
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection), plus the project's form library and schema library, if any. Keep its validation rules.
2. Choose what the task needs: an error summary for longer forms, async checks, multi-step handling. Leave out the rest.

3. Set up the timing (patternSpec.do, frameworkPatterns.errorTiming), with the project's form library if it has one (integrationPatterns). Hide and disable sections that don't apply (frameworkPatterns.conditionalSection).
4. Write the messages: what is wrong and how to fix it, with the field's label (implementationDetails.messages).
5. Handle submit as in frameworkPatterns.submitErrors, and the busy state while sending (implementationDetails.sending).
6. Add async checks and multi-step handling if the form needs them (implementationDetails).
7. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard and a screen reader, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

patternSpec.problem: Errors that appear too early nag people while they type or read the form; errors that appear too late waste their time; errors that only some people can perceive lock the others out; and a form that clears or blocks what people entered makes them start again.
patternSpec.solution: Show a format error when someone leaves a field they typed in, and "required" errors only after a submit attempt, when every field is checked; once a field shows an error, check it on every input, so the error goes as soon as it is fixed. Show each error in text next to its field, connected with aria-describedby and aria-invalid. On a failed submit, move focus to an error summary that links to each field, or to the first invalid field on a short form. Use the project's form library when it has one, and the browser's constraint validation with the app's own messages when it doesn't.
do: Check a field someone typed in when they leave it, and every field on a submit attempt; hold "required" errors back until that attempt
Hide and disable a section that doesn't apply, and clear its errors when it hides

After a reset that wasn't cancelled, rebuild everything worked out from the values, as on page load: the errors and the summary go, no field counts as typed in, "required" waits again, and sections follow their answers
Once a field shows an error, check it on every input, so the error goes as soon as the value is right
Say what is wrong and how to fix it, using the field's label: "Enter an email address in the correct format, like name@example.com"
Keep everything people typed when showing errors
Show each error in text next to its field, in its aria-describedby, with aria-invalid="true" on the field
On a failed submit, move focus to the error summary's heading on a longer form, or to the first invalid field on a short one
Keep the submit button enabled until sending starts, then use aria-disabled and ignore another press
Mark required and optional fields in words, and put the required attribute on required fields
Set novalidate from script, so the app's messages replace the browser's, and the browser still checks the form without script
Wait for a pause before async checks, and count only the latest answer
In multi-step forms, check each step before moving on, move focus to the new step's heading, and fill in what was already given
dont: Show errors while someone types in a field that has none yet, or for fields they only tabbed through
Show "required" before a submit attempt, even for a field someone typed in and emptied
Check fields in a section that doesn't apply, or skip fields only because they're visually hidden: custom controls often hide their native input and still need its validation
Show "Passwords must match" while the confirmation is still being typed
Disable the submit button before a submit attempt, or with the disabled attribute while sending
Make field errors live regions, or combine role="alert" with aria-live="polite"
Clear a field because its value is wrong
Rely on color alone, or color an asterisk like an error
Put the expected format only in a placeholder, which disappears on typing
Use browser alert() dialogs for errors
Reveal private facts in errors or availability checks, such as whether an email has an account
Show a library's technical messages, such as "field_email failed pattern"
examples: Email: someone types "john@" and moves on; the error "Enter an email address in the correct format, like name@example.com" appears. As they type "example.com", it goes the moment the address is complete.

Required field: someone tabs past an empty Full name field to read the form, and nothing appears. They type a letter, delete it, and move on: still nothing. They submit, and "Enter your full name" appears, with focus on the field.

A section that doesn't always apply: "I'm buying for a company" shows the Company details section and enables it; unticked, the section hides, is disabled, and loses its errors, and the form can be sent without it.
Password confirmation: nothing shows while the confirmation is typed. If it doesn't match when they leave it, "Passwords must match" appears, and goes as soon as it matches.

Username availability: after a 500 ms pause in typing, "Checking…" in the status region, then "Username available" or "That username is taken. Try another" next to the field. An older answer that arrives late is ignored.
Checkout, a longer form: a submit with three errors shows the summary "There is a problem" at the top, with links to the three fields, and focus on its heading.
Multi-step form: Next checks the step; with errors it stays, and without, focus moves to the next step's heading "Delivery address", with the name from step 1 already filled in.
Card number: the hint says "The 16 digits on the front of your card"; spaces typed between groups are accepted and removed.
Date of birth: three fields, day, month, and year, in the person's locale order, rather than a date picker.
antiPatterns: Errors on page load, before any interaction.
An error on focus, before anything is typed.
A submit button that stays disabled until the form is valid, so nobody can find out what is missing.
An error that stays after the value is fixed, until the field is left.
A submit that only shows the first error, so people fix the form one error at a time.

requirements.1.3.1: Errors and hints are connected to their fields with aria-describedby.
requirements.1.4.1: Errors are text, not only a color.
requirements.2.4.3: A failed submit moves focus to the summary or the first invalid field; a new step moves it to the step's heading.
requirements.2.4.11: With a sticky header, scroll-padding-top keeps a focused field clear of it.
requirements.3.3.2: Required and optional fields say so in words.
requirements.3.3.3: Errors say how to fix the problem.
requirements.3.3.4: A legal, financial, or data-changing submission can be reviewed and corrected before it is final.
requirements.3.3.7: Multi-step forms don't ask again for information given in an earlier step.
requirements.4.1.3: Results, such as "Sending…" or an async check, are announced through one polite status region.

accessibility.announcements: Focus is the announcement on a failed submit: the summary's heading or the first invalid field is read, with its error. No live region repeats the errors. An error that appears when someone leaves a field may be announced once through the form's one polite status region; role="alert" is never used on field errors.

focusManagement.failedSubmit: Focus moves to the error summary's heading (tabindex="-1") on a longer form, or to the first invalid field on a short one.
focusManagement.summaryLinks: Each summary link goes to its field (#id), and following it moves focus there (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit).
focusManagement.newStep: A new step in a multi-step form moves focus to its heading.

integrationPatterns.note: Set up the project's form library, if it has one, to give this timing. These notes name versions; check the project's version.
integrationPatterns.reactHookForm7: The defaults (mode: "onSubmit", reValidateMode: "onChange") show errors after a submit attempt and clear them as people fix them. To also show format errors before that, call trigger(name) on blur when getFieldState(name).isDirty is true and the field isn't empty, and on change while getFieldState(name).invalid is true: before the first submit, the defaults don't check a field again as it changes. Until formState.isSubmitted, clear a field's error with clearErrors(name) when it's emptied, since "required" waits for a submit attempt. mode: "onTouched" comes close, but also flags required fields someone only tabbed through.
integrationPatterns.veeValidate4: Set when fields are checked with validateOnBlur, validateOnChange, validateOnInput, and validateOnModelUpdate, globally with configure() or per field, and show a required error only once the form's submitCount is above 0. Version 3's mode: "lazy" is gone.
integrationPatterns.angularForms: Show a control's error when the form was submitted, or when the control is dirty and touched and its error isn't required. The value updates on each input, so the error goes as soon as it's fixed.
integrationPatterns.schemaLibraries: With a schema library, such as Zod, Valibot, or Yup, keep the rules in the schema, and map its messages to the field errors and the summary.
integrationPatterns.withoutLibrary: The browser's constraint validation: required, type, pattern, min, max, and minlength in the markup, read through field.validity, with the app's own messages (frameworkPatterns).

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

errorTiming.description: When errors appear, with the browser's constraint validation: a field someone typed in is checked when they leave it, a field with an error on every input, "required" held back until a submit attempt, and novalidate set from script. afterReset() runs code after a reset that wasn't cancelled; the reset clears the errors and forgets which fields were typed in.

submitErrors.description: The error summary for longer forms, and the submit handler: the submit attempt recorded, every field checked, the form not sent with errors, and focus on the summary's heading or the first invalid field. A reset hides and empties the summary and forgets the submit attempt.
submitErrors.html: There is a problem

conditionalSection.description: A section that only some answers need: hidden and disabled while it doesn't apply, so its fields leave validation and the form data, with its errors cleared when it hides. It follows its answer on load, on change, and after a reset.
conditionalSection.html: Company details

implementationDetails.timing: Nothing shows while the form loads, or while someone tabs through it. A field someone typed in is checked when they leave it, for format errors. "Required" errors wait for a submit attempt, even for a field someone typed in and emptied; after that attempt, every error shows, required ones included. Once a field shows an error, it is checked on every input, so the error goes the moment the value is right; emptied before a submit attempt, it shows no error. Dependent fields, such as a password confirmation, follow the same rule. CSS :user-invalid comes close: in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit it matched after typing an invalid value and leaving, and after a submit attempt, also with novalidate, and not after tabbing past an empty field. But it also matches a required field someone typed in and emptied, as they leave it (checked). So style aria-invalid, which follows the app's timing; use :user-invalid only when the browser's validity is the only source.
implementationDetails.reset: Most forms don't need a reset button: it's easy to press by mistake, and it loses everything typed. Apps often reset a form from script after sending it, though, so these rules hold either way. After a reset that wasn't cancelled, everything worked out from the values is rebuilt from the restored values, as on page load: the errors and the summary go, no field counts as typed in, "required" waits for the next submit attempt, and sections follow their answers. The form puts its values back only after its reset event, without input or change events, and a listener after yours can still cancel the reset, so wait for the event to finish and check defaultPrevented first (afterReset() in frameworkPatterns.errorTiming).
implementationDetails.conditionalFields: Put a section that only some answers need in a <fieldset>, and while it doesn't apply, make it hidden and disabled (frameworkPatterns.conditionalSection). Disabled fields are left out of validation and of the form data (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit), so they can't block the submit. Clear the section's errors when it hides. The section follows its answer on page load, on change, and after a reset, which puts the answer back without a change event and leaves the section's own hidden and disabled as they were. Don't skip fields only because they're visually hidden: custom controls often hide their native input and still need its validation.
implementationDetails.messages: Say what is wrong and how to fix it, with the field's label: "Enter your full name", "Enter an email address in the correct format, like name@example.com". Errors from the server show the same way, at the field they belong to, or in the summary for the form as a whole. Never reveal private facts: "Email already registered" tells anyone who has an account; availability checks are for public names, such as usernames or handles, and the server rate-limits them.
implementationDetails.requiredFields: Say "required" or "optional" in words: when most fields are required, mark the optional ones "(optional)" and say so at the top. If the design uses an asterisk, explain it at the top of the form, and don't color it like an error. Required fields have the required attribute.
implementationDetails.sending: While the form is sent, the submit button gets aria-disabled="true" and ignores another press, and the status region says "Sending…". The disabled attribute would drop focus from the button, or from a field where someone pressed Enter. On success, go on; on failure, keep everything typed, show the error, and make the button work again.
implementationDetails.asyncChecks: Check after typing pauses (about 500 ms, suggested), say "Checking…" in the status region, and count only the latest request's answer: number each request, or abort the previous one with an AbortController.
implementationDetails.multiStep: Check each step when someone tries to move on, as a submit, with only that step's fields (its fieldset's elements); earlier steps stay enabled, so they're sent with the form, and a step that an answer skips is disabled like a conditional section. On a new step, move focus to its heading (tabindex="-1"), so its title and instructions are read, and update the page title, such as "Delivery address, step 2 of 4". Don't ask again for something given in an earlier step: fill it in, or offer it to choose (WCAG 2.2 3.3.7). Before a legal, financial, or data-changing submission, let people review and correct everything (WCAG 3.3.4).
implementationDetails.formats: Accept common formats and normalize them, such as spaces in card numbers and dashes in phone numbers. Show the expected format in hint text, not in a placeholder. Dates follow the person's locale; for a date people know by heart, such as a birthday, three fields (day, month, and year) work better than a picker.
implementationDetails.stickyHeaders: Focusing a field scrolls it into view; with a sticky header, scroll-padding-top on the scrolling element keeps it clear of the header (WCAG 2.4.11).

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

edgeCases.layoutShift: When an error appears as someone leaves a field to press the submit button, the button moves under the pointer before the mouse is released, and the click is lost (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). The form is invalid anyway, and the error shows; to keep the click, keep room for one error line under the fields above the button.
edgeCases.conditionalFields: A section that doesn't apply is hidden and disabled, so it isn't checked or sent, and its errors go when it hides (implementationDetails.conditionalFields).
edgeCases.formReset: A reset that wasn't cancelled starts over, as on page load; a cancelled one changes nothing (implementationDetails.reset).
edgeCases.autofillAndPaste: Autofilled and pasted values count as typed.
edgeCases.serverRendered: A form that reloads with errors from the server puts the summary at the top, moves focus to it on load, and starts the page title with "Error:".
edgeCases.severalForms: Each form on a page has its own summary and status region.

must: Use the project's form library and schema library when it has them, and keep their rules
Show errors when a field someone typed in is left, or on a submit attempt, and clear them as soon as they are fixed
Move focus to the summary or the first invalid field on a failed submit
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a form or schema library without asking
Show errors while someone types in a field without one, or for fields they only tabbed through, or "required" before a submit attempt
Check fields in a section that doesn't apply; hide and disable the section instead
Disable the submit button before a submit attempt, or use the disabled attribute while sending
Reveal whether an account exists in an error or an availability check
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: Tabbing through the form without typing shows no errors
A field someone typed in shows a format error when they leave it, and the error goes as soon as the value is right
"Required" errors appear only after a submit attempt, even for a field someone typed in and emptied, and then for every empty required field
A section that doesn't apply is hidden and disabled, so it never blocks the submit; its errors go when it hides, and it follows its answer on load and after a reset
A form reset clears the errors and the summary, forgets which fields were typed in, and holds "required" back again; a cancelled reset changes nothing
A failed submit moves focus to the error summary's heading on a longer form, or to the first invalid field on a short one, and each summary link moves focus to its field
Errors are text next to their fields, connected with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and say how to fix the problem
No field error is a live region, and screen readers hear each error once
The submit button stays enabled until sending starts, then uses aria-disabled, keeps focus, and ignores another press
With script, the browser's own error messages don't appear; without it, the browser still checks the form
Required and optional fields say so in words
Async checks wait for a pause, say "Checking…", and only the latest answer counts
Multi-step forms move focus to each step's heading and never ask twice for the same information
A focused field is never hidden under a sticky header
A form library, if the project has one, is set up to give the same timing
